papers.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
papers.problem: AI agents paste long raw tool outputs into their context, which slows them down and hides the useful parts.
papers.fix: Coca-Cola squeezes tool outputs into compact hidden tokens, cutting token use 70.01%-89.24% and runtime 24.45%-55.97% while improving task scores.
papers.practicalUseCase: If agents can read compressed tool results, they run faster and cheaper, so test latent compression in search agents.
papers.limitation: Tests covered only web-search agents on four question-answering benchmarks and two model families.

papers.title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.problem: Offline AI apps update through signed knowledge packs, but a signature does not prove the vectors match the text.
papers.fix: A loose vector check leaves up to 5.5% of queries exposed, and attacks cut correct answers from 0.75 to 0.39.
papers.practicalUseCase: A valid signature can still hide a hijacked search index, so verify quantisation codes instead of loose vector tolerances.
papers.limitation: Tests used five corpora, two embedding models, and a small Raspberry Pi 5 setup.

papers.title: StepX-OPD: Rethinking Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Diffusion Models
papers.problem: Image models need many skills and few-step sampling, but building them in two stages loses quality and wastes time.
papers.fix: StepX-OPD trains both together, beats the forty-step Flow-OPD model with four steps, and uses about 37% fewer GPU-hours on SD3.5-Medium.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you train image models, merging skill training and step cutting can save compute, so try one combined stage.
papers.limitation: Authors tested two models, SD3.5-Medium and FLUX.1-dev, and saw unwanted prompt words appear inside images.

papers.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
papers.problem: AI-guided program search is slow because the model writes long text reasoning every round.
papers.fix: SwarmEvolve reaches in a median of 3 to 8 minutes the best scores that other methods reach in 60 minutes.
papers.practicalUseCase: Swarms that think without writing text can cut search cost, so try them for slow optimization jobs.
papers.limitation: Results come from 21 mathematical and scientific computing problems, so other tasks may differ.

papers.title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
papers.problem: Nobody had a large, graded set of open research problems to test whether AI can solve them.
papers.fix: Without web access, AI agents rediscovered at most 7 of 40 solved problems, and web wins mostly copied published answers.
papers.practicalUseCase: AI agents rarely solve fresh research problems alone, so treat their research claims with doubt and check the source.
papers.limitation: The agent test used only the 50-problem HQ-50 subset, all in mathematics.

papers.title: Islamic Social Financial Instruments and Sustainable Community Development: Evidence Synthesis on Community Resilience
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Research on zakat, waqf, and sadaqah is scattered, so it is unclear how they build community resilience.
papers.fix: Across 93 studies, zakat gives short-term relief, waqf builds long-term assets, and sadaqah gives flexible emergency help.
papers.practicalUseCase: Combined ZISWAF models work best, so charities should join all three tools and add good governance and digital systems.
papers.limitation: This review pools published studies from 2010 to 2025, so it shows patterns, not proven cause.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks set up sustainability committees, but it is unclear whether they drive real environmental action.
papers.fix: In Islamic banks, committees lift overall scores but not green products, while conventional banks improve on all four areas.
papers.practicalUseCase: Islamic bank committees may mostly signal effort, so regulators should check products and innovation, not just scores.
papers.limitation: The data cover banks in emerging markets only and show links, not cause.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Nobody had mapped how sustainability sukuk issuance grew or what sets its size.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts give larger issues than sale-based ones.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers who want bigger sustainability sukuk should favour equity-based contracts, since costly second party opinions shrink issue size.
papers.limitation: Data end in 2022, and the study shows what links to issue size, not what causes it.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lack evidence on whether AI and big data improve competitiveness and sustainable development.
papers.fix: AI use, big data skills, and data management link to better competitiveness and sustainability, but staff skills help only competitiveness.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks that invest in AI and data management gain an edge, so fund these before only training staff.
papers.limitation: A one-time survey of 214 managers at 15 Jordanian Islamic banks shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks lack clear evidence on whether ICT, high-tech exports, and institutions drive growth in dual banking systems.
papers.fix: ICT is the strongest driver of expansion across 218 banks in 12 countries, and high-tech exports help only alongside ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks and regulators should fund digital infrastructure first, because ICT drives growth and unlocks the value of national innovation.
papers.limitation: Data cover 2010 to 2023 in 12 countries, so results may not fit other markets.

papers.title: Procrastination among US college students: Prevalence and impact relative to common health and life issues
papers.problem: Nobody knew how common student procrastination is compared with other health and life issues.
papers.fix: Procrastination affects 72.3% of 65,950 US students, and hurts grades for 45.4%, about 2.8 times more than finances.
papers.practicalUseCase: Procrastination hurts more students than most health issues, so colleges should treat it as a top problem.
papers.limitation: Students self-reported in a US survey, so the data show how common it is, not why.

papers.title: “The significance of context”: Fit, friction, and function in the work lives of early career academics with ADHD
papers.problem: Little data shows how ADHD shapes work life for early-career academics.
papers.fix: Interviews show academia can reward ADHD, but social and institutional pressure often blocks it.
papers.practicalUseCase: Fit between your brain and your workplace matters, so universities should adjust environments, and you should seek supportive teams.
papers.limitation: This is an interview study with a small group, so it shows experiences, not rates.
